- Zone_F3_Z01 (Core_mid) Zone_Air_Temperature_Sensor — available
- Zone_F3_Z01 cooling/heating temperature setpoints — available (essentially flat, ~25.2 °C / ~18.6 °C before and after July 2018, Δ<0.06 °C)
- VAV_F3_Z01 Damper_Position_Setpoint — available (≈0.23 pre vs ≈0.25 post, Δ+0.015, essentially unchanged)
- Zone_F3_Z01 zone temperatures of all other zones — available

The graph does declare `Zone_F3_Z01_Electric_Power_Sensor` and `Zone_F3_Z01_CO2_Sensor`, but **neither is present in the timeseries store** (the catalog has no Power or CO2 stream for F3_Z01). The only zone-level physical measurement I have is a single air-temperature sensor.

What the data do show:
- F3_Z01 temperature rose ≈0.63 °C pre/post July 2018, while F3_Z02 rose ≈0.62 °C and F4_Z01 ≈0.38 °C, and the rest of the building rose ≈0.1–0.7 °C. The rise is not unique to F3_Z01.
- Neither the cooling SP (Δ+0.03 °C), heating SP (Δ−0.06 °C), nor the damper-position SP (Δ+0.015) changed between halves, so the controller isn't doing materially more for F3_Z01.
- A sensor reading that has drifted upward would look identical to a real local load increase if I only have that one temperature measurement; I have no independent measurement in the same zone to cross-reference.

To distinguish "local load change" from "zone sensor fault" I would need streams that exist in the graph but are not exposed:
